articles.title: Kolkata's Jhal Muri Gets Edible Paper Twist At Hyderabad's Anaganaga Restaurant
articles.excerpt: The Jubilee Hills Telugu restaurant serves the Kolkata street snack on a sheet of edible paper, part of a menu that reworks familiar Indian dishes at a 200-cover venue built on years of culinary research.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers, the dish shows how a beloved Kolkata street snack is being reimagined inside a premium Telugu restaurant in Hyderabad, carrying regional food memories across state lines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Mini North-East in Chennai: The Grocery Stores Keeping Migrant Kitchens Stocked
articles.excerpt: Around 20 northeastern stores line the lanes behind Velachery's Phoenix Mall alone, flying in chayote leaves, napakpi and bamboo shoot for Chennai's eight-state northeastern community.
articles.image_caption: Koyambedu wholesale market in Chennai. The city's north-eastern grocery stores stock produce flown in for migrant kitchens.
articles.nri_angle: The Chennai stores mirror what diaspora grocery stores do abroad: keep a home kitchen possible thousands of kilometres from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mizoram, India's Ginger Capital, Bets on GI-Tagged Crop for Export Markets
articles.excerpt: NITI Aayog recognised Mizoram as the Ginger Capital of India in 2025. Behind the title sit GI-tagged Thingpui and Thinglaidum varieties with oleoresin at 6-8%, Rs 137.72 crore paid to farmers in 2025, and four new processing units planned in Champhai.
articles.nri_angle: Ginger is a foundation ingredient in diaspora Indian kitchens; GI-tagged Mizo varieties give overseas shoppers a named origin - low-fibre, high-oleoresin Thingpui and Thinglaidum - to look for as processed products reach export shelves.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Seizes 9.4 Tonnes of Paneer and Khoya Worth Rs 28.4 Lakh in Pune
articles.excerpt: The Maharashtra FDA seized 9,000 kg of paneer and 440 kg of khoya at Bavdhan, Kasba Peth and Bibwewadi on October 19, finding consignments from Karnataka transported and stored without proper temperature control, days before Diwali.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families ordering Diwali sweets for relatives in Pune should check that khoya and paneer stock is refrigerated and labelled, and can report suspect stock via the FSSAI grievance portal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pune Restaurant Bills to Rise 10-15% Before Diwali as Costs Surge
articles.excerpt: Maharashtra restaurants will revise menus in the next eight to 10 days as LPG, vegetables, dairy, wages and rent climb — some dishes could rise 18%.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families visiting Pune for Diwali will pay 10-15% more for restaurant meals, adding Rs 200-300 to a typical Rs 2,000 family dinner.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rupee Beer Launches Diwali Campaign Linking Diyas, Food and Beer
articles.excerpt: The Portland-based Indian-inspired brewer's 'Light One. Pour One.' campaign pairs lighting a diya with sharing food and beer for Diwali 2026.
articles.image_caption: Diwali diyas. Rupee Beer's 2026 Diwali campaign, 'Light One. Pour One.', pairs lighting a diya with sharing food and beer.
articles.nri_angle: The campaign speaks directly to Indian-American Diwali gatherings in the US, framing beer brewed for Indian food as part of the festive table.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Katrina Mirpuri Shares Family Diwali Feast Recipes With Tesco for London Homes
articles.excerpt: The journalist known as Curry Bradshaw sets out eight vegetarian family dishes, from potato chaat and saag paneer to tadka daal and salted lassi, with Tesco Clubcard prices running to 10 November 2026.
articles.image_caption: A Diwali thali. Katrina Mirpuri shared her family's Diwali feast recipes with Tesco for London homes.
articles.nri_angle: For British Indians in London, Mirpuri's grandmother-taught menu offers a complete home Diwali table from mainstream supermarket staples.

articles.title: Sweet Sellers Face Shelf-Life Labels for Loose Mithai Ahead of Diwali
articles.excerpt: Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand now require use-by dates on unpackaged sweets — closing a disclosure gap, and adding per-batch compliance work for small halwais at peak season.
articles.image_caption: Mithai on display for sale. Uttar Pradesh now requires use-by dates on loose sweets sold from open trays.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora buyers get a concrete check for family buying loose mithai in India: each tray must now show its own use-by date — from Oct 15 in UP and Oct 26 in Uttarakhand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Uttar Pradesh requires use-by dates for loose sweets.
Uttarakhand mandates manufacturing and expiry dates for unpackaged sweets.

articles.title: Sushi Sits Beside Chaat at Delhi's Dussehra Melas This Festival Season
articles.excerpt: India Today found sushi served alongside chaat and pav bhaji at Delhi's Ramlila fairs, where the traditional stalls — chaat, jalebis and kulfi at Subhash Maidan — still anchor the mela menu.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora festival-goers in the US, whose Navratri and Diwali fairs widened their menus years ago, will recognise Delhi's melas making the same move at larger scale, with sushi as the newest stall next to chaat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nepal Bans Priyagold Biscuits After India Flags Cattle-Feed Bran
articles.excerpt: Nepal halted imports, sales and distribution of Priyagold biscuits and ordered a recall of stocks after India's FSSAI suspended maker Surya Food and Agro's licence and moved to prosecute over alleged use of cattle feed bran.
articles.nri_angle: Priyagold packs are sold in South Asian grocery stores abroad; diaspora shoppers should check the manufacturer name, Surya Food and Agro Ltd, on the pack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chef Deepak Mishra to Open Bungalow 147, a 130-Seat Indian Restaurant in a Heritage Williamstown Bank
articles.excerpt: The former Langham Melbourne executive chef is bringing Odisha and Bengal cooking to an 1869 waterfront bank building in Melbourne's inner west this summer.
articles.image_caption: Chef Deepak Mishra stands inside Bungalow 147 by the Bay during its fit-out in Williamstown. The 130-seat restaurant opens this summer inside an 1869 heritage-listed former bank on the Hobsons Bay waterfront.
articles.nri_angle: A senior Indian hotel chef is opening Melbourne's most ambitious new Indian restaurant, centred on underrepresented Odisha and Bengal cuisines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric Crosses Rs 23,000 a Quintal in Erode as Drought Cuts Planting
articles.excerpt: Finger turmeric hit its highest level in recent years at Perundurai as drought in Maharashtra, Telangana and Tamil Nadu cut planted area by up to 30% in some regions and futures pointed to tight supplies into 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Wholesale turmeric prices in Erode have surged on drought and thin arrivals, signalling higher retail spice costs for Indian households abroad in the months ahead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amar Kale Paints Karnataka in Chilli and Turmeric for a World Record
articles.excerpt: The Dharwad artist's 175.82-square-metre spice painting of Karnataka and the Hampi Chariot is the largest ever, made from 11 kg of two kitchen spices.
articles.nri_angle: The work is made from turmeric and chilli, the two spices present in every diaspora Indian kitchen.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mississauga's Mughal Mahal, Known for Amritsari Kulcha, Is Expanding to Brampton
articles.excerpt: The Punjabi restaurant, trading in Mississauga since 1990, announced a Brampton location on social media. No opening date has been set.
articles.image_caption: Amritsari kulcha, the tandoor-baked stuffed flatbread Mughal Mahal is known for (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: Brampton's Punjabi diaspora gains a local branch of a Mississauga kulcha institution many already drive across Peel Region to reach.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flavors of Bollywood Puts Indian Cuisine Centre Stage at New York City's Biggest Food Festival
articles.excerpt: Chefs Maneet Chauhan and Vijay Kumar hosted a sold-out debut of street food, regional specialties and Bollywood spectacle at the NYC Wine & Food Festival, weeks ahead of Diwali.

articles.nri_angle: A sold-out, top-tier slot for Indian cuisine at New York's biggest food festival gives Indian-American food culture a mainstream stage in the run-up to Diwali.

articles.title: India Ships the Harvest, Not the Meal: Value-Added Foods Still a Thin Slice of Food Exports
articles.excerpt: Processed foods are only about a fifth of India's $50 billion-plus food exports, but Diwali demand and a ready-to-eat surge show where the value is moving.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers are the demand base pushing Indian packaged and ready-to-eat foods from ethnic aisles into mainstream US, Gulf and European supermarkets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA Shuts Fortis Hospital Kitchen, Six Domino's Outlets in Crackdown
articles.excerpt: Inspectors reported cockroaches, fungus and rusted knives at the Sodexo kitchen inside Fortis Hospital, Mulund, as the FDA suspended 25 food establishments and four manufacturing units statewide.
articles.nri_angle: The crackdown is a reminder for families in India and abroad that hospital and chain-restaurant kitchens are only as safe as their last inspection.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Plant or Animal on the Plate? Sleep Research Says Timing Matters as Much as the Menu
articles.excerpt: A 20-person lab study found no difference between meat and vegetarian dinners, while cohort data links plant-forward eating to lower insomnia risk and late eating to 43% higher odds of night waking.
articles.nri_angle: A common Indian household dinner debate answered with study numbers, including absolute insomnia rates.

articles.title: Bengaluru Sisters Turn Grandmother's Donne Biryani Into a Rs 10 Crore Business
articles.excerpt: Ramya and Shweta Ravi's RNR Donne Biryani crossed 10,000 orders in its first month in 2020 and has clocked Rs 10 crore since, built on a leaf-pouch Karnataka biryani most of India had never tried.
articles.nri_angle: A regional Karnataka dish diaspora readers rarely find abroad, built into a delivery-first brand on a family recipe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Kap's Cafe Dubai, Where Masala Chai Costs Rs 500
articles.excerpt: Kapil Sharma's Al Karama cafe, themed on his Netflix show, sells pani puri for about Rs 800 and pasta for AED 62 — a premium take on Indian street food in Dubai.
articles.nri_angle: For Indians in Dubai and visiting tourists, Kap's Cafe turns familiar street food into a premium, show-themed outing in Al Karama.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashwagandha and Turmeric Lead India's Ayurveda Export Push — Evidence Is the Entry Price
articles.excerpt: On Ayurveda Day 2026, India's export council says the botanicals are ready for global markets; the multi-herb formulations behind them still need the clinical trials to catch up.
articles.image_caption: Turmeric powder sits in a mortar alongside other spices and ingredients on a wooden board. Ashwagandha and turmeric lead India's push to turn Ayurvedic botanicals into standardised global exports.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora consumers are core buyers of ashwagandha and turmeric supplements abroad; standardisation and traceability decide which Indian products stay on US and EU shelves.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Top Chef Alum Rasika Venkatesa Opens Mythily, Progressive South Indian Restaurant in Williamsburg
articles.excerpt: Named for her Chennai grandmother, the 45-seat Mythily reworks Tamil home cooking with French Laundry technique — and a Kickstarter-funded build-out behind it.
articles.image_caption: The dining room at Mythily in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, is set with wooden tables, benches and plants on a shelf against a white brick wall. Chef Rasika Venkatesa opened the 45-seat South Indian restaurant at 129 Havemeyer Street on September 30.
articles.nri_angle: A Chennai-born chef is giving New York diaspora diners regionally specific Tamil cooking at fine-dining level in Williamsburg.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Asked Followers for Diwali Sweets. They Sent a ₹1.69 Lakh TV — on Cash-on-Delivery
articles.excerpt: Madurai creator Veeramani shared his address for a box of sweets and was flooded with fake COD orders for TVs, fridges and phones, until appeals failed and he left home.
articles.nri_angle: A reminder for Diwali gifting season: send prepaid, confirm with the recipient, and never publish a home address to receive gifts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paul & Mike and Tata Starbucks Turn Coffee Into Diwali Chocolate
articles.excerpt: The limited-edition collection pairs a Caramel Macchiato chocolate with Saffron Pista and Pista Katli, in a 12-piece box priced at Rs 990 at select Starbucks stores across India.
articles.nri_angle: A store-bought Diwali gift in India at Rs 990 that diaspora readers can have family pick up locally, avoiding international shipping.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Seeks FSSAI Response on Non-Dairy Products Sold as Paneer
articles.excerpt: A bench has given the Centre, FSSAI and Delhi government six weeks to reply to a plea for inspections and disclosure, but declined an interim festive-season enforcement drive.
articles.image_caption: Cubes of paneer are pictured on a plate. The Delhi High Court has sought responses from FSSAI and the Centre on non-dairy products being sold as paneer.
articles.nri_angle: The Delhi case concerns products sold in India and sets no rule for imported paneer; its disclosure argument is the part relevant to anyone buying paneer labelled as dairy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.excerpt: In Delhi for the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, the former UK prime minister revisited a favourite Bengali Market institution with his mother-in-law Sudha Murty and Swati Maliwal — for chaat, lassi, laddoos and rasmalai.

articles.title: India's Restaurant Sector Bets on Niche Cuisines Over Generic Menus
articles.excerpt: Travellers returning with specific tastes, a food services market heading past $125 billion by 2030, and diners ordering 20% more unique cuisines are pushing Indian restaurants toward sharp, single-cuisine concepts.
articles.nri_angle: India's shift to niche, regional and single-cuisine restaurants mirrors what diaspora diners already seek abroad — and shapes what NRI visitors and returning restaurateurs will find and build at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.nri_angle: A new family-run Indian restaurant gives southwest Fort Worth's Indian community a local dining and catering option, with South Indian and Hyderabadi dishes beyond the standard curry-house menu.
